statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen inside this horizon, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any published hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor. Stress rises to the upper elevated band because the US-Iran tanker campaign has become two-sided: the IRGC now claims retaliatory strikes on three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels, a claim CENTCOM has not confirmed, alongside a near-10% weekly crude gain and hawkish September rate pricing.
recommendation: Tail holds a 4-7% closed-venue floor across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress opens at 57%, eases to 54% through the dormant Sunday overnight window and rebuilds to a 65% peak as the horizon tracks toward the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen, crossing from the elevated into the high band only in the final two slots. The danger window is left empty because no evidence-based intraday window can be defined while quoting is suspended. Tail remains far below the block threshold; the scores would be rescored on the observed reopening path, with orderly two-way retracement decaying them quickly and repeated extension after failed pullbacks the first genuine amplifier.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through a second day of the CME weekend halt as Iran claims its own tanker strikes in Hormuz, turning the US campaign two-sided while crude holds a near-10% weekly gain
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, three hours after the final slot of this forecast, so the last print remains the only anchor and no published hour can contain observable price action.

The material change since the previous assessment is that Iran's response has moved from words to a claimed kinetic counter-strike. The Jerusalem Post reports that the IRGC says it targeted three oil tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz together with three US-affiliated ships, in retaliation for the three Iranian tankers struck earlier on Saturday, and warned shipping against routes it has not authorised. Iran's military command added that if the naval blockade and harassment of Iranian ships continue, its strikes against US military vessels in the region will be more severe than before. CENTCOM has not confirmed the Iranian claims. CBS News live coverage carries the same claim and records the earlier US action, in which Adm. Brad Cooper said that if the IRGC shoots at two US ships the response would be to take out three of theirs. The tanker-for-tanker cycle is therefore now two-sided and unresolved, which is the reason Stress rises rather than Tail.

Cross-asset context remains conflicted rather than aligned, which under the published definitions raises Stress and lowers conviction without amplifying Tail. WTI trades at $91.48 after a weekly gain of more than 9%, its strongest week since mid-July, with Brent at $96.28 and US diesel at a record $5.85 a gallon; only 102 vessels transited the Strait last week against more than 130 a day before the conflict. Yet equity volatility has barely transmitted any of this: VIX closed Friday at 14.53, up 1.47% on the day and still under 15. The Friday tape was internally split, with semiconductors broadly bid on the AI memory cycle while Apple, Microsoft and Tesla fell. Rates remain the second unresolved input, with the 2-year at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77% on the latest H.15 release after the August payroll surprise pushed September pricing hawkish, and with public pressure on the Fed adding noise rather than information.

None of this can be expressed in price until the venue reopens. Tail therefore stays at a closed-venue floor of 5%, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and widening to 7% only as the horizon approaches the venue timeline, which keeps every published hour mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress carries the escalation instead, opening at 57% and building to 65% in the final slots where the largest volume of unpriced weekend information meets the shortest remaining interval to a live quote. The US Monday macro calendar is empty, so the first scheduled checkpoint after the reopen is Tuesday's NFIB and New York Fed inflation-expectations pair, ahead of PPI on Thursday and CPI on Friday.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the closing hour of the Friday payroll session and the first twenty-three hours of the CME weekend halt. The 20:00 UTC hour on 4 September was scored at Tail 12% and Stress 48% under a mixed mode as the index gave back its highs and recovered into the settle. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5% under a normal mode, with Stress flat at 38% through the overnight window. Stress then climbed steadily from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 52% by 19:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed and the tanker strikes were verified. Every one of the 24 slots is available from published Claude assessments and every one maps to EA_ON and green.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which does not end until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, three hours after the final published slot, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-7% closed-venue floor, easing through the dormant middle of the weekend and widening only as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress opens at 57%, reaches a 54% low in the quietest overnight hours and rebuilds to a 65% peak into Sunday evening, crossing from the elevated into the high band in the final two slots on a now two-sided and unresolved Hormuz tanker campaign, a near-10% weekly crude gain, record US diesel and hawkish September rate pricing, none of which has met a quote since Friday. Confidence declines from 86% to 77% across the horizon because later slots rest on progressively older evidence during an actively developing sequence. The reopening auction is the first hour in which structure can be scored: orderly two-way retracement would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier.
